Este tema dominó las conversaciones entre líderes gubernamentales y empresariales durante el segundo día del Foro de la Nueva Economía de Bloomberg en Nueva Delhi, el miércoles. Ver más: Los países donde más crecerán las exportaciones de bienes en América Latina en 2026, según la Cepal El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de la India, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, declaró ante los asistentes que los países de potencia media deben ser proactivos a la hora de relacionarse entre sí y “encontrar la manera de lograr avances en los temas que les interesan”. Funcionarios suizos y canadienses hablaron sobre la necesidad de diversificar los socios comerciales y fortalecer la resiliencia de las cadenas de suministro. El ex primer ministro británico Rishi Sunak afirmó que una estrategia de supervivencia para las naciones consistía en aprovechar sus ventajas competitivas en el comercio para “volverse indispensables”. El desafío al que se enfrentan las potencias medianas, a menudo descritas como naciones con influencia global, pero sin estatus de superpotencia, se ha agudizado en los últimos años a medida que el presidente estadounidense Donald Trump trastocó las alianzas tradicionales y se debilitaron instituciones como la Organización del Tratado del Atlántico Norte. A principios de este año, el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, hizo un llamamiento a estos países para que se unieran en respuesta al colapso del llamado orden basado en normas liderado por Estados Unidos. Entre los mayores desafíos que enfrentan las potencias medianas se encuentra el debilitamiento de cadenas de suministro que antes eran confiables. La ofensiva arancelaria de Trump ha estrangulado el acceso de muchos países al mercado de consumo más grande del mundo. La inestabilidad en Oriente Medio y la guerra en Ucrania han obligado a muchas naciones a buscar fuentes alternativas de energía y alimentos, mientras que el dominio de Pekín en minerales críticos e insumos tecnológicos clave ha generado nuevos problemas para los directores ejecutivos y los líderes mundiales. “Nos hemos alejado de una era donde se eliminaron las barreras, donde existía la libre circulación de dinero y de mercancías, para entrar en una era en la que se sufre y se ve afectada por la instrumentalización de todo lo posible”, declaró Yuvraj Narayan, director ejecutivo del gigante logístico DP World, en el evento de Bloomberg. Hizo hincapié en los nuevos riesgos que se presentan en los principales puntos estratégicos, desde el estrecho de Ormuz hasta el canal de Panamá y el estrecho de Malaca. “Si bien en la época que acaba de terminar podría haber invertido mil millones de dólares en cadenas de suministro, ahora voy a considerar invertir casi el doble”, dijo. La negociadora comercial suiza, Helene Budliger Artieda, afirmó que su país se ha centrado en la resiliencia y la diversificación de contratos tras las interrupciones en la cadena de suministro, y declaró el miércoles ante un panel que ha estado “muy ocupada viajando y firmando acuerdos de libre comercio”. Ver más: Comercio mundial sorprende al alza pese a los choques en Medio Oriente: estos países destacan en América Latina “Como país pequeño, no podemos evitar los obstáculos”, dijo Artieda. “No queremos fabricar todo en Suiza. No tendría ningún sentido, ya que somos un país pequeño con una economía mediana”. Para ilustrar su carácter “indispensable”, Sunak puso como ejemplo a los Países Bajos, que controlan de facto el mercado de los equipos más avanzados para la fabricación de chips. Alemania, Corea del Sur y Japón también dominan segmentos cruciales de la cadena de suministro de chips, afirmó. “Si eres una potencia intermedia, debes encontrar la manera de volverte indispensable y convertirte en un punto de estrangulamiento”, dijo. Para Canadá, instrumentalizar sus ventajas estratégicas no era una opción, declaró la ministra de Asuntos Exteriores, Anita Anand. “Lo que considero importante, al menos desde la perspectiva canadiense —y me gustaría que otras potencias medianas también adoptaran esta idea— es que nunca utilizaremos nuestras ventajas competitivas como arma”, afirmó. Para el ministro de Comercio de la India, Piyush Goyal, impulsar la autosuficiencia era fundamental. Afirmó que la estrategia cobró mayor urgencia a raíz de la pandemia de Covid-19, tras revelarse la dependencia de la India de las vacunas importadas. “En todos los países donde hicimos pedidos de equipos de protección personal, kits para la Covid-19 o vacunas, nos decepcionaron estrepitosamente”, afirmó. Finalmente, India se convirtió en un importante fabricante y exportador de vacunas. Artieda, el negociador comercial suizo, planteó la estrategia de otra manera: “Lo más importante es mantener la calma y comer chocolate suizo”. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Top 25 roundup: Florida, Tramell Jones Jr. upset No. 7 Texas
item.description: Tramell Jones Jr. passed for 155 yards and a pair of touchdowns in his first career start, as the Gators scored 24 unanswered points on the way to a 27-24 win over the No. 7 Longhorns in a Southeastern Conference game in Austin, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tramell Jones Jr. passed for 155 yards and a pair of touchdowns in his first career start, as the Gators scored 24 unanswered points on the way to a 27-24 win over the No. 7 Longhorns in a Southeastern Conference game in Austin, Texas. Florida (5-2, 3-2) also got 91 yards on 25 carries from Jadan Baugh, including an 11-yard TD run with 6:22 remaining to put the Gators up 27-17. Texas' Arch Manning hit Cam Coleman for a 9-yard scoring pass with 4:21 left to cut into the deficit. The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2) had another chance to tie or win the game, but Manning fumbled when he was sacked by Florida's Myles Graham. Kanye Clark fell on the ball with 1:58 to play. Manning finished with 173 yards passing, completing 14 of 20 attempts, but Texas had only 272 total yards compared with 313 for Florida. The Longhorns, the top-ranked team in the nation eight days ago, dropped their second straight contest. No. 4 Ohio State 19, No. 5 Indiana 15 Jeremiah Smith was bottled up for three quarters but his 38-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter helped the Buckeyes hold off the Hoosiers in Big Ten action in Bloomington, Ind. The Hoosiers (6-1, 3-1) had their 22-game winning streak end when a fourth-and-4 pass at the Ohio State 27-yard line was incomplete when Nick Marsh stepped out of bounds in the end zone while making the catch with 1:02 left. Ohio State (6-1, 4-0) led 13-7 early in the fourth, when on fourth-and-1 from the Indiana 38, Smith recorded his 39th career receiving touchdown to tie Michigan's Braylon Edwards for the Big Ten record. The two-point conversion failed as the Buckeyes led 19-7 lead with 12:46 remaining, but Indiana responded with a 19-yard catch by Marsh from Josh Hoover and a two-point pass to Turbo Richard to make it 19-15. Smith had four catches for 68 yards. Julian Sayin was 15 of 29 for 235 yards with a TD and two interceptions before being injured in the fourth. He was sporting a sling late in the game, and Buckeyes coach Ryan Day said Sayin would miss several weeks. No. 22 LSU 31, No. 16 Mississippi State 0 Sam Leavitt passed for 289 yards and four touchdowns as the Tigers routed the visiting Bulldogs in Baton Rouge, La. Leavitt, who entered the game with an SEC-worst eight interceptions, threw none against Mississippi State as he completed 31 of 38 passes. Jackson Harris caught two touchdown passes for the Tigers (5-2, 2-2 SEC), whose defense stopped all five of the short-handed Bulldogs' fourth-down attempts. Mississippi State (4-2, 2-2) was without quarterback Kamario Taylor, the SEC leader in passing touchdowns and yards per game, and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell, both because of injuries. Redshirt freshman Billy Puckett started in place of Taylor and threw for 121 yards and an interception on 16-of-26 passing. Anthony Evans III, who entered the game leading the SEC in receptions per game and receiving yards per game, finished with seven catches for 40 yards. No. 24 SMU 23, Virginia 13 Kevin Jennings passed for 246 yards and two touchdowns to lead the host Mustangs past the Cavaliers in Dallas. Jennings' second touchdown pass, a 37-yarder to Jalen Hale early in the fourth quarter that provided the game's final margin, tied him with Ben Hicks (2016-18) for second place in school history with 71 career touchdown passes, one shy of the record set by Tanner Mordecai (2021-22). Jennings finished 23-for-36 with no interceptions. Kendrick Raphael rushed for 124 yards, Yannick Smith had five catches for 87 yards, and former SMU soccer player Brendan Baird kicked the first three field goals of his career as the Mustangs (5-1, 3-1 Atlantic Coast Conference) won their third consecutive game and improved to 10-0 at home in conference play since joining the league in 2024. Beau Pribula had 137 yards on 13-of-22 passing and ran for 25 yards and a touchdown for the Cavaliers (4-3, 2-2), who fell to 0-3 away from home this season. Will Bettridge kicked a pair of field goals for Virginia's other points. No. 25 Northwestern 24, Michigan State 21 Jackson Kleather's 34-yard field goal with two seconds remaining lifted the Wildcats to a comeback win over the Spartans in East Lansing, Mich. The Wildcats (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten) prevented an upset by the Spartans (2-5, 0-4) and former Northwestern coach Pat Fitzgerald when Matthew Smith blocked a go-ahead field goal attempt from 33 yards by Liam Boyd with one minute left in the fourth quarter. Northwestern then drove eight plays and 64 yards to set up Kleather's game-winning kick. Aidan Chiles completed 18 of 27 passes for 226 yards, and Caleb Komolafe ran for 67 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries for Northwestern, which is ranked for the first time since 2020. Alessio Milivojevic completed 19 of 30 passes for 216 yards and two touchdowns for Michigan State. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eagles place QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on IR
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve on Saturday because of a superficial blood clot in his left calf, and the condition will sideline the three-time Pro Bowl quarterback indefinitely, according to multiple reports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia Eagles placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve on Saturday because of a superficial blood clot in his left calf, and the condition will sideline the three-time Pro Bowl quarterback indefinitely, according to multiple reports. The Eagles' decision to put Hurts on IR came after consultations with several doctors and experts, ESPN and the NFL Network reported. Hurts must miss at least four games, beginning Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, followed by matchups with the Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants. Philadelphia (2-3), which has lost three straight, then has a Week 10 bye, when the Eagles will reevaluate Hurts' health and the team's outlook, per ESPN and NFL Network. The Eagles believe the blood clot is treatable, but Hurts' medical team will determine when the 28-year-old can return to play, according to the reports. In five games this season, Hurts has passed for 933 yards and eight touchdowns, with three interceptions. Doctors discovered the blood clot during an Oct. 10 ultrasound after Hurts sustained a calf injury against the Los Angeles Rams on Oct. 4. They cleared him to play against Jacksonville the following day, when he completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown without an interception in a 19-17 loss. However, a follow-up ultrasound Wednesday showed the clot moving, prompting further evaluation. Eagles backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers, and rookie Cole Payton was promoted to backup. Philadelphia also signed quarterback Joe Milton off Dallas' practice squad. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ohio State QB Julian Sayin injured, out several weeks
item.description: Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin will miss several weeks after injuring his throwing arm during the Buckeyes' 19-15 victory over host Indiana on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin will miss several weeks after injuring his throwing arm during the Buckeyes' 19-15 victory over host Indiana on Saturday afternoon. Ohio State coach Ryan Day revealed the timeline but didn't detail specifics of the injury. "I don't have a ton of details, but He will probably be out for several weeks so we'll have to come up with a plan," Day said in his postgame press conference. Sayin sustained the injury with just over eight minutes left in the fourth quarter when Indiana's Mario Landino slammed into Sayin's right arm between the elbow and shoulder. Sayin fumbled the ball and it was recovered by teammate Phillip Daniels. A short time later, Sayin headed to the locker room with the arm noticeably limp. He returned sporting a sling with 3:35 remaining. Sayin completed 15 of 29 passes for 235 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions before exiting. Luke Fahey replaced him and threw two incompletions. Sayin has passed for 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions this season. He finished fourth in Heisman Trophy balloting last season when he threw for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Fahey is 9-for-13 passing for 203 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Ohio State has a bye next weekend before visiting No. 19 Southern California on Oct. 31. --Field Level Media

item.title: Patriots activate star WR A.J. Brown off injured reserve
item.description: The New England Patriots activated wide receiver A.J. Brown from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New England Patriots activated wide receiver A.J. Brown from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the New York Jets. Brown missed the past four games after sustaining a high-ankle sprain during New England's season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The three-time Pro Bowl selection was traded to the Patriots this offseason after four seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles. For his career, he has totaled 527 receptions, 8,055 receiving yards and 56 receiving touchdowns. The Patriots (3-2) have rebounded from a 1-2 start with consecutive victories over the Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders. They will try to extend their winning streak Sunday against the Jets (2-3). --Field Level Media

item.title: Inter earn 3-1 comeback win at Bologna, Roma beat Genoa 2-0
item.description: Inter Milan came from a goal down to beat Bologna 3-1 in Serie A on Saturday, maintaining their unbeaten start and going two points clear at the top.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Inter Milan came from a goal down to beat Bologna 3-1 in Serie A on Saturday, maintaining their unbeaten start and going two points clear at the top. Inter, who suffered a [USN:L6N45Z15P TEXT:"shock"] home loss to Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday, went behind in the 10th minute to a goal from Tommaso Pobega but equalised through Marcus Thuram against the run of play just before halftime. Second-half goals from Carlos Augusto and Ange-Yoan Bonny helped secure the win that lifted them to 19 points with their sixth victory in seven league matches. Cristian Chivu's side are two points ahead of AS Roma, 2-0 winners over visitors Genoa thanks to second-half goals from Santiago Castro and Emanuele Lulli. Third-placed Lazio, who have 16 points, visit Juventus on Sunday after AC Milan in sixth spot with 12 host Atalanta. Juve are seventh with 11 points.

item.title: Horse racing-Loughnane becomes Britain's youngest champion jockey since 1923
item.description: Ireland's Billy Loughnane was crowned Britain's champion jockey at Ascot on Saturday, making the 20-year-old the youngest rider to win the title in more than a century.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ireland's Billy Loughnane was crowned Britain's champion jockey at Ascot on Saturday, making the 20-year-old the youngest rider to win the title in more than a century. Loughnane beat fellow Irishman and five-time champion Oisin Murphy, 31, to become the youngest winner since Charlie Elliott in 1923. “Nearly four years ago when I was going up to Newcastle for my first ride, my aim then was just to have a few winners really," Loughnane said on a Great British Racing media call earlier this week. "If anyone had said that day that four years later I’d be where I am now I’d have said they were absolutely crazy." The 20-year-old, who has recorded more than 220 victories this year, will now turn his sights to Gordon Richards' 1947 record of 269 winners in a calendar year.

item.title: Dembele atones for penalty miss in PSG win at Strasbourg
item.description: Paris St Germain coach Luis Enrique gambled with a much-changed starting lineup and was almost made to pay as the Ligue 1 champions rode their luck to claim a 3-1 victory at RC Strasbourg on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paris St Germain coach Luis Enrique gambled with a much-changed starting lineup and was almost made to pay as the Ligue 1 champions rode their luck to claim a 3-1 victory at RC Strasbourg on Saturday. Gio Reyna put the home side ahead in the first half and they might have added to that tally but for the brilliance of PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov. Ousmane Dembele missed a penalty for the visitors in the second half but minutes later they were level through Ilya Zabarnyi before Dembele scored five minutes from the end of the 90 and Desire Doue netted a third in added time. The win moves PSG top of the table on goals scored with 14 points from seven games, ahead of Lille, who drew 1-1 at home to Brest, and AS Monaco before they visit Lorient on Sunday. Luis Enrique made eight changes to his team from the midweek Champions League win at Manchester City with only Safonov, Warren Zaïre-Emery and Maghnes Akliouche selected again. Safonov was superb as he thwarted Strasbourg several times before PSG earned the points late on. They finished the game with 10 men as defender Nuno Mendes was withdrawn with no substitutions remaining. "He felt a little thing (on his thigh) and we decided to play with one less player so as not to take risks," Luis Enrique told reporters. DEMBELE PENALTY MISS Dembele missed a second-half penalty with the score at 1-0 to Strasbourg, but put that disappointment behind him to net one goal, assist another and play a part in the third. "I told him if you play 25 minutes and give an assist and score a goal, you don't need to play more. That's enough," Luis Enrique said. Dembele's penalty miss meant PSG have scored one of their four spot-kicks this season, a poor record from 12 yards. "He was angry because he missed the penalty. It's true, we have a statistic (from penalties) that is a little difficult to take," Luis Enrique added. "We have many players who can shoot but it is true that we lack a specialist (penalty-taker)." Lille were held by Brest as 40-year-old Olivier Giroud equalised for the hosts from the penalty spot after 64 minutes. Brest took an early lead through Mama Balde and climb to eighth on nine points. Lens rose to seventh on 10 points after a 3-1 win at second-bottom Troyes. They took the lead through an Adrien Monfray own goal after 13 minutes before Odsonne Edouard and Ruben Aguilar secured the points after Timothe Nkada equalised for the hosts.

item.title: ローマ教皇が退院、肺腺がん手術後の検査良好 日曜の祈りに参加へ
item.description:
Joshua McElwee
[バチカン市 １７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Joshua McElwee

[バチカン市 １７日 ロイター] - 肺腺がんの手術を受けたローマ教皇レオ１４世が１７日、入院していたローマの病院を退院した。教皇庁（バチカン）によると、１８日の日曜の祈りに参加する予定という。

教皇はローマのジェメリ病院の外で手を振って見送りの人々に応えながら、自力で歩いて待機していた車に向かった。

教皇は１３日に、がん組織を全て除去するため右肺の下葉を切除する手術を受けた。手術後の経過は良好で１６日にはロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談していた。

医師団は１７日、血液検査や胸部画像検査を行った結果、教皇は退院できる状態にあり、日常の活動も自立して行うことができると述べた。

教皇は１１月６─１７日にウルグアイ、アルゼンチン、ペルーを訪問する予定。

item.title: Prominent Guatemalan anti-corruption lawyer killed in shooting
item.description: Guatemalan lawyer Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa, known for his high-profile fight against corruption in the Central American country, died after being shot on Saturday by two men while visiting a sports center in Guatemala City, a crime condemned by President Bernardo Arevalo.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Menchu
item.content:encoded: Guatemalan lawyer Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa, known for his high-profile fight against corruption in the Central American country, died after being shot on Saturday by two men while visiting a sports center in Guatemala City, a crime condemned by President Bernardo Arevalo. Solorzano Foppa was a 43-year-old former prosecutor and anti-corruption lawyer who denounced wrongdoing by some of Guatemala's most powerful politicians, business leaders and companies, and in 2023 briefly joined the defense team of a prominent journalist. Shortly after the attack, Guatemalan police reported that they had detained two men and seized a carbine-style firearm and a motorcycle. According to the police, the arrests and seizure of the weapon were in connection with the case. "I strongly condemn the cowardly murder of former prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa. Both the direct perpetrators and those who ordered the crime must face the full weight of the law," Arevalo said on his official X account. He added that he had instructed his government to coordinate with the relevant authorities to solve the crime. "Those who believe that terror can intimidate the people of Guatemala and the government I lead are mistaken. In honor of Foppa, in honor of our homeland, in honor of justice." The lawyer was known for his anti-corruption work as head of the Criminal Investigations Directorate within the Public Prosecutor's Office, and later as head of Guatemala's tax authority, the SAT, from 2016 to 2018, when he helped prosecute dozens of powerful Guatemalan business figures and recover unpaid taxes. In 2025, Solorzano Foppa alleged a connection between the Barrio 18 gang and the National Unity of Hope party, as well as links between criminal gangs and the judicial system. In 2023, he briefly joined the defense team of Guatemalan journalist Jose Ruben Zamora, who has become an international symbol of resistance to the criminalization of journalism and the erosion of judicial independence in Central America. Solorzano Foppa had to leave the Zamora case after being accused by the Public Prosecutor's Office of obstructing the proceedings and destroying or concealing information, a charge he denied but ultimately accepted as part of a plea agreement, saying he did not believe he would receive a fair trial.

item.title: Lebanon says military delegation will press for halt to Israeli attacks at US talks
item.description: A Lebanese military delegation will present Beirut's demands for an end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon at a trilateral meeting in Tampa, Florida, on October 20, the Lebanese presidency said in a post on X on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Lebanese military delegation will present Beirut's demands for an end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon at a trilateral meeting in Tampa, Florida, on October 20, the Lebanese presidency said in a post on X on Saturday. Lebanon and Israel have held a number of direct talks in recent months, aimed at ending hostilities since a new war erupted on March 2 between Israel and the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah, triggered by the wider regional conflict . Under a deal reached through US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks, Beirut vowed to disarm Hezbollah, which would in turn lead to Israeli troops gradually withdrawing from Lebanon. But Hezbollah has refused to disarm as long as Israeli forces remain on Lebanese land, and Israel has continued striking southern Lebanon.

item.title: Capitals score 4 straight goals, double up Devils
item.description: Ilya Protas scored the tiebreaking goal early in the second period Saturday afternoon for the host Washington Capitals, who rode a four-goal surge to a 4-2 win over the New Jersey Devils.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ilya Protas scored the tiebreaking goal early in the second period Saturday afternoon for the host Washington Capitals, who rode a four-goal surge to a 4-2 win over the New Jersey Devils. Ryan Leonard scored in the first before Dylan Strome and Boone Jenner added goals in the second for the Capitals, who have won two straight. Goaltender Logan Thompson made 29 saves. Arseny Gritsyuk had a goal in the first and Timo Meier scored in the final minute of the third for the Devils, whose two-game winning streak ended. Goalie Jake Allen recorded 21 saves as New Jersey sustained its fourth multi-goal defeat of the season. The Devils opened the scoring just after a power play expired at the 10:04 mark of the first, when Gritsyuk's shot from behind the left faceoff circle clipped off Thompson and trickled into the net. The Capitals tied the score six minutes later with a power-play goal fueled by Leonard's impressive effort. Leonard took a drop pass from Jakob Chychrun in front of the Washington net, raced up the ice, weaved between the Devils' Evan Rodrigues and Luke Hughes and shifted the puck before burying it into the right corner of the net with 3:18 left. Protas gave the Capitals the lead for good by capping another end-to-end rush 1:16 into the second. Alex Ovechkin sent a pass beyond the reach of Devils defenseman Jonas Siegenthaler and over the stick of Stefan Noesen to Protas, who sent a shot over Allen's glove shoulder. The Capitals padded the lead just 3:20 later. Strome and Jordan Kyrou exchanged the puck between the faceoff circles before Kyrou fed Strome at the edge of the crease, where the center shuffled the puck before flicking a shot over the glove of a sprawling Allen. Jenner closed out the decisive outburst with 8:46 left in the second period. Vincent Desharnais' shot from above the right faceoff circle glanced off the stick of Devils defenseman Johnathan Kovacevic to Jenner, who beat Allen from point-blank range. The Devils were 0-for-3 on the power play before Meier scored a power-play tally with 19 seconds left in the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Mercedes planta cara a Porsche con un SUV eléctrico de alto rendimiento
item.description: La versión básica ofrecerá una autonomía de hasta 668 kilómetros (415 millas), mientras que los modelos de gama alta podrán recorrer 700 km con una sola carga.
item.dc:creator: Laura Malsch
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Mercedes-Benz Group AG ha presentado el primer SUV eléctrico desarrollado íntegramente por su marca AMG, apostando por que el alto rendimiento le ayudará a destacar en un mercado de lujo cada vez más saturado. Con un precio de salida de 113.050 euros (US$127.060), la versión básica del SUV AMG GT sale a la venta este martes, mientras que en primavera le seguirán dos opciones de gama superior. El modelo supone un desafío directo al Cayenne eléctrico de Porsche AG, que se presentó el pasado mes de noviembre. En su intento por impresionar a los compradores que buscan prestaciones, el SUV AMG GT supera ligeramente en potencia a su rival, gracias a sus tres motores de flujo axial y su batería de 800 voltios, que generan hasta 1.169 caballos de potencia. La versión básica ofrecerá una autonomía de hasta 668 kilómetros (415 millas), mientras que los modelos de gama alta podrán recorrer 700 km con una sola carga. La variante más alta de la gama puede alcanzar los 100 kilómetros por hora en 2,5 segundos. Ver más: América Latina supera el millón de vehículos electrificados: estos países lideran en autos y buses en circulación Aunque está dirigido a consumidores que buscan una conducción de alto rendimiento, el vehículo también compite con otros SUV eléctricos recién presentados por Jaguar Land Rover —con el primer Range Rover eléctrico— y por Bentley Motors Ltd., de Volkswagen AG. Un SUV de gama alta podría contribuir a reforzar la rentabilidad a medida que aumenta la presión sobre el negocio principal de Mercedes, pero solo si logra convencer a los compradores de que la electrificación no se produce a costa de la velocidad y el sonido. Esto se suma a una gran serie de lanzamientos de productos de Mercedes, con 40 modelos nuevos o actualizados previstos para 2027, muchos de ellos dirigidos a los segmentos más caros de la marca. «No es ningún secreto que los vehículos de gama alta contribuyen de manera desproporcionada a nuestra rentabilidad», afirmó Mathias Geisen, miembro del consejo de administración responsable de Ventas y Experiencia del Cliente, en el acto de presentación celebrado en Stuttgart. Se trata del primer SUV que AMG ha fabricado de forma propia, a diferencia de los SUV eléctricos AMG existentes, que son versiones de gama alta de modelos de Mercedes. Tras el lanzamiento del AMG GT Coupé de cuatro puertas a principios de este año, el SUV GT, que se fabricará en la planta de Mercedes en Sindelfingen, es el segundo modelo basado en la plataforma eléctrica de AMG. El proyecto llega en un momento crucial. Las ventas de vehículos eléctricos a batería de Mercedes alcanzaron un récord en el tercer trimestre de este año, con un aumento del 61%, a pesar de que las ventas totales de automóviles descendieron. Las ventas de las versiones eléctricas del CLA y del GLC ya han tenido una gran acogida entre los compradores y están agotadas en Europa para el resto de 2026. En China, donde las ventas totales descendieron más de un 30% en el tercer trimestre, la demanda de una versión del GLC desarrollada específicamente para atraer a los compradores locales es “mejor de lo esperado”, afirmó Geisen. Si continúan las tendencias de crecimiento del tercer trimestre en Europa y EE. UU., “probablemente registraremos a finales de año nuestras mayores ventas fuera de China desde 2019″, afirmó. Ver más: El dinero que se ahorra en gasolina con un carro eléctrico en América Latina en 2026, según Olacde Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Ukrainian foreign minister says Russian-held town is a 'death trap' with starving residents
item.description: Andrii Sybiha urged international organizations to help evacuate residents.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Saturday that Russian occupying forces were turning the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a "death trap" gripped by starvation, and urged international organisations to help evacuate its residents. Sybiha made his comments on X a day after Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged, in a [USN:L8N4621IK TEXT:"conversation with Pope Leo"], to cooperate in delivering vital supplies into the town in southern Ukraine's Kherson region. "Russians are trying to turn the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a death trap. The hospital has run out of medicine. Dozens of bodies lie in the streets or in homes, as Russians forbid residents from burying them," Sybiha wrote. "Families are starving, surviving on leftover garden vegetables, preserves and even snails ... Ukraine has repeatedly called for safe evacuation and international humanitarian access. These appeals cannot remain unanswered." The Kremlin acknowledged in September that Oleshky had [USN:R4N45100U TEXT:"critical problems"] with food and medical supplies but said Russia's military was working to resolve them. Ukraine's military has twice used drones to [USN:L1N45Q03T TEXT:"deliver food"] and medicine to the town. Sybiha urged the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and other organisations to "secure safe evacuation corridors and immediate humanitarian access." Oleshky lies on the east side of the Dnipro River in Kherson region, which Russian forces mostly occupied soon after the 2022 invasion. A Ukrainian counteroffensive later recaptured large chunks of territory, including the city of Kherson. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy described the situation in Oleshky this week as [USN:L8N45Y0E8 TEXT:""genocide.""] Oleshky had a pre-war population of 24,000 people and is now home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. Local prosecutors said on Saturday Russian forces dropped aerial bombs on the city of Kherson, on the opposite bank of the Dnipro from Oleshky, killing an ambulance driver and wounding 40 people.

item.title: Muere en ataque a balazos reconocido exfiscal anticorrupción de Guatemala, crimen causa indignación
item.description: El abogado guatemalteco Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, reconocido por su lucha contra la corrupción en el país centroamericano, falleció tras ser atacado el sábado a balazos por dos dos hombres cuando dirigía a un equipo de fútbol durante un partido en un centro deportivo en la capital de Guatemala, en un crimen que causó indignación y fue condenado por defensores de derechos humanos y el presidente Bernardo Arévalo.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Menchu
item.content:encoded: El abogado guatemalteco Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, reconocido por su lucha contra la corrupción en el país centroamericano, falleció tras ser atacado el sábado a balazos por dos dos hombres cuando dirigía a un equipo de fútbol durante un partido en un centro deportivo en la capital de Guatemala, en un crimen que causó indignación y fue condenado por defensores de derechos humanos y el presidente Bernardo Arévalo. El ministro de Gobernación de Guatemala, Marco Antonio Villeda, dijo que una de las dos personas detenidas poco después del homicidio y que presuntamente habrían participado en el ataque era un exmilitar que había solicitado su baja del Ejército en febrero del 2019. En total, dijo el funcionario, se presume la participación de cuatro personas en el crimen. Los dos atacantes se acercaron a Solórzano Foppa cuando el abogado se alejó de sus escoltas y su hijo para moverse en el campo mientras dirigía al equipo de fútbol, dijo Villeda, quien no aventuró un móvil del sobre el homicidio. "Todavía no estamos en una etapa de certezas; estamos en una etapa de recolección de evidencias, análisis de indicios para construir una investigación sólida", dijo. "No vamos a adelantar en este momento conclusiones, ni tampoco vamos a excluir ninguna hipótesis ya que la verdad debe prevalecer y establecerse con pruebas", subrayó. El abogado, de 43 años, quien denunció la corrupción de empresarios y políticos, formó parte por poco tiempo en 2023 de la defensa del periodista guatemalteco [USN:L1N3Z81J8 TEXT:"José Rubén Zamora"], actualmente en arresto domiciliario, pero tuvo que dejar el caso tras ser acusado por el Ministerio Público de Consuelo Porras de obstaculizar el proceso y destruir u ocultar información. La policía había informado que había incautado un arma de fuego tipo carabina y una motocicleta al momento de detener a los dos presuntos atacantes. El homicidio causó revuelo en Guatemala y pedidos de justicia. La relatora especial de la ONU sobre la independencia de jueces y abogados, Margaret Satterthwaite, demandó en su cuenta de X el esclarecimiento de lo sucedido y que se "protejan a las autoridades de justicia del país". La embajada de Estados Unidos en Guatemala calificó en su cuenta de X de "atroz" lo sucedido y añadió que esperaba una investigación "completa y transparente que permita esclarecer los hechos". Solórzano Foppa se destacó por su lucha contra la corrupción cuando fue jefe de la Dirección de Investigaciones Criminalísticas en el Ministerio Público, así como cuando fungió entre 2016 y 2018 como jefe de la autoridad tributaria, SAT, cuando llevó a prisión y obligó a decenas de poderosos empresarios guatemaltecos a pagar impuestos. En 2025, Solórzano Foppa denunció una presunta vinculación entre la pandilla del Barrio 18 y el partido Unidad Nacional de la Esperanza (UNE) así como la existencia de vínculos entre las pandillas y el sistema judicial. Villeda dijo que la seguridad que recibía el exfiscal por parte del Estado desde 2010 se había incrementado en 2025 debido a su perfil político, pero no dio detalles, aunque aseguró que el abogado no había denunciado recientemente amenazas.

item.title: Nuggets G/F Julian Strawther (knee) sidelined at least six weeks
item.description: Denver Nuggets swingman Julian Strawther will miss at least six weeks after suffering a left knee sprain during a preseason game last week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Denver Nuggets swingman Julian Strawther will miss at least six weeks after suffering a left knee sprain during a preseason game last week. Strawther was injured Wednesday against the Los Angeles Clippers and helped off the court. There were fears the injury was season-ending before an MRI exam detected a sprain. Strawther will be re-examined in six weeks, when an updated timetable will likely be revealed. The 24-year-old Strawther has averaged 7.1 points and 1.8 rebounds in 172 games (18 starts) over three NBA seasons. Last season, he averaged 7.2 points and 2.0 rebounds in 57 games (14 starts) and shot a career-best 46.7% from the field. He is eligible through Monday to sign a rookie-scale extension with the Nuggets. Strawther was a first-round pick (29th overall) by Denver out of Gonzaga in 2023. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lions play through tears in honour of teammate Andrews
item.description: Several of the players from South Africa’s Lions side could not hold back tears as they paid an emotional tribute to teammate Hyron Andrews ahead of their Champions Cup fixture against French side La Rochelle on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Several of the players from South Africa’s Lions side could not hold back tears as they paid an emotional tribute to teammate Hyron Andrews ahead of their Champions Cup fixture against French side La Rochelle on Saturday. Andrews, 31, was [USN:L1N4620GN TEXT:"found unresponsive at the team’s hotel"] on the Ile de Re on Friday and could not be resuscitated. No cause of death has yet been determined. A statement from South Africa Rugby said he "died after falling at the team hotel". The Lions decided to play the fixture in honour of Andrews and put in a spirited display but went down 31-14 to the more fancied home side. La Rochelle fans had formed a guard of honour to welcome the visitors at the stadium. Andrews' number 5 jersey was laid out in front of his teammates as an impeccably observed moment of silence was held at the Stade Marcel-Deflandre. Ruan Delport, selected to play in the second row, instead wore the number 24, leaving Andrews' number free. South Africans on the La Rochelle side, Dillyn Leyds and Salmaan Moerat, presented a special number 5 jersey to Lions coach Ivan Van Rooyen, while the ground erupted into applause in the fifth minute of the match. The Lions also have two United Rugby Championship fixtures in Scotland on their European tour, at Edinburgh next Friday and Glasgow Warriors the week after.

item.title: Barcelona keep perfect LaLiga record with five-goal romp at Betis
item.description: Barcelona's LaLiga juggernaut rolled into Seville on Saturday and left with the scoreboard smoking, as the leaders beat Real Betis 5-2 to make it nine wins from nine and stretch their blistering league tally to 39 goals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Barcelona's LaLiga juggernaut rolled into Seville on Saturday and left with the scoreboard smoking, as the leaders beat Real Betis 5-2 to make it nine wins from nine and stretch their blistering league tally to 39 goals. Lamine Yamal lit the fuse with a dazzling opener before Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and substitute Dani Olmo joined the party, while Valentin Gomez and Ez Abde replied for Betis, who played much of the second half with 10 men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for headbutting Lamine. Barca moved to 27 points, five above Atletico who won 1-0 at Espanyol, while third-placed Betis have 19 and Real Madrid sit fourth on 18 before welcoming Sevilla on Sunday, Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini made eight changes from the side that beat Porto 3-2 in the Champions League, resting several key players including Antony, Marc Bartra, Natan and Isco with a midweek European meeting against Feyenoord in mind. Yet the hosts still made Barca sweat before the visitors eventually found space, rhythm and, after Betis were reduced to 10 men, plenty of room to turn the match into another attacking exhibition. Lamine opened the scoring in the 10th minute in familiar style, gliding in from the right before whipping a left-footed strike from the edge of the box into the top corner. Betis levelled in the 27th when Pablo Fornals collected a rebound on the right and clipped a cross into the middle for Gomez, who rose highest to head past goalkeeper Joan Garcia. Barcelona reclaimed the lead in the 41st minute when Spain captain Rodri powered in a header from Fermin Lopez's corner. Betis thought they had equalised three minutes later through Gio Lo Celso's spectacular swivelling volley from outside the box, but the effort was ruled out after Cucho Hernandez was adjudged to have handled earlier in the build-up. Jesus, signed from Arsenal in the close season, had a goal disallowed for offside shortly after the break but was not kept waiting long. In the 51st, Lamine darted down the right and squared for the Brazilian to finish neatly inside the area. A minute later Abde pulled one back on the counter, sliding a low shot inside the right post, but Betis' celebrations turned sour when Bernal was shown a straight red card following a scuffle. Lamine was booked for his part in the altercation. Barcelona made it 4-2 in the 63rd minute when Alvaro Valles failed to deal with Lamine's free kick and Pau Cubarsi headed the loose ball back across goal for Garcia to tap in. Olmo completed the rout in the 81st minute, curling a right-footed shot into the top corner from outside the box. Atletico won 1-0 at Espanyol, with Baena coming off the bench to deliver the late sting in a cagey match in Barcelona. Both sides struck the post in a tight tactical contest before Atletico's substitutes combined in the 89th, Julian Alvarez bursting down the left and squaring for Baena, who drove a fierce strike into the top corner from the edge of the box.

item.title: Commanders rule out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt, 3 others vs. 49ers
item.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice all week and was ruled out Saturday for Monday night's away game against the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn told reporters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice all week and was ruled out Saturday for Monday night's away game against the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn told reporters. Along with Croskey-Merritt, Quinn said quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), edge rusher Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) and defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) will not travel with the team for the game in Santa Clara, Calif. Quinn said Croskey-Merritt reinjured the groin he hurt in August. "That's harder, on the same injury," he said. "We'll work really hard to get him back." Croskey-Merritt leads the Commanders with 239 rushing yards and has two rushing touchdowns. He missed the final two preseason games with a groin injury. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest) are expected to share running back duties, though both have been limited in practice. Jeremy McNichols, who began the season on injured reserve with a quadriceps injury, will travel with the team and could be activated Monday. Wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who missed last Sunday's 27-27 tie against the New York Giants, practiced Saturday, along with Terry McLaurin (hamstring). The pair have combined for 32 receptions, 373 yards and four scores this season. Cornerback Trey Amos (ankle) and safety Nick Cross (illness) were full participants in practice and could return Monday. Amos has been on injured reserve, while Cross has been out since Week 2. --Field Level Media

item.title: Steelers' DK Metcalf off injury report, Pat Freiermuth added
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers removed one player from the injury report and added another on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Steelers removed one player from the injury report and added another on Saturday. Wide receiver DK Metcalf was taken off the report by the Steelers (3-2) for Sunday's game against the host Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4). He was questionable due to an illness. Tight end Pat Freiermuth, however, was added to the injury report as questionable due to a calf injury. Metcalf, Freiermuth and running back Jaylen Warren are tied for the team lead in catches with 19. Freiermuth has a club-best four touchdown receptions to go along with 169 receiving yards, while Metcalf has 225 receiving yards and one score. --Field Level Media

item.title: City's flying start comes at a cost, with Haaland limping off
item.description: Manchester City maintained their perfect Premier League start with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday, but the sight of a badly limping Erling Haaland heading straight down the tunnel added another concern to those already hanging over the club.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City maintained their perfect Premier League start with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday, but the sight of a badly limping Erling Haaland heading straight down the tunnel added another concern to those already hanging over the club. City are appealing a ruling that they breached 114 Premier League financial rules and deny wrongdoing, but the uncertainty off the pitch has done little to disrupt them on it. Enzo Maresca's side have won seven league games from seven for their best-ever start to a Premier League season. Maresca became the first manager to win his opening seven Premier League games in charge as City bounced back from Wednesday's Champions League defeat by Paris St Germain, his first meaningful loss as City boss. Haaland struck twice after Phil Foden's first goal of the season had been cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, with the Norwegian's second his 100th non-penalty Premier League goal, reached in a record 139 appearances. He was denied a hat-trick by an offside in the build-up before Zian Flemming's stoppage-time penalty made the scoreline closer than the game felt. But victory came at a potentially heavy cost during a punishing stretch of four games in 10 days. While Maresca had made six changes to his team from Wednesday, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly all went off injured, while Antoine Semenyo was also limping badly at the final whistle. "Unfortunately, in 10 minutes, we had four, five players (hurt)," Maresca said. "I don't have any news at the moment." Haaland made a beeline for the tunnel rather than staying to applaud supporters, unusual for the striker, with Semenyo hobbling off not far behind. DEFIANT VOICE "I don't know (Haaland's injury)," Maresca said. "I asked him. He said that he was okay. So hopefully, it's nothing serious." The uncertainty surrounding City has hardly dampened the mood among their supporters, who were in defiant voice at the Etihad as a stadium-record 60,817 watched the game. They loudly booed the Premier League anthem before kick-off and waved inflatable bananas, reviving a City tradition dating from their days outside the top flight in the 1980s. Supporters turned the prospect of possible relegation as a sanction into gallows humour, chanting "You're going down with the City!" at the travelling Ipswich fans. Outside the stadium, vendors did brisk business selling bananas and T-shirts carrying anti-charge slogans, including "Stick your charges where the sun don't shine" and "City til I die." "The environment was very good," Maresca said. "They just said to me that today was a record attendance, so that's also a nice thing. The fans, the club, the players, we are all together in this journey, and this is the best feeling for everyone." Maresca has said several times since the team reconvened after the international break that he has instructed his players to shut out external criticism as the club appeals the guilty verdict. Captain Ruben Dias said earlier in the week that "it's almost impossible to avoid seeing something, even us being as private as we can be and just doing our own lives on your phone. It's impossible to avoid everything." Maresca praised his players for their focus. "The players, they need to be worried about people inside the club and about me for the credit I give to them, and they are not worried about people that can judge them from outside. "But inside, I promise you that the players they are happy. The club gives credit to the players. I give credit to the players. So this is for us the most important thing." Asked about managing against City with everything that has happened off the pitch, Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil shrugged and said: "No. Just us against City trying to win. Bananas, no bananas, makes no difference."

item.title: Zelenski afirma que las restricciones de velocidad de Starlink parecen deliberadas
item.description: Las tensiones se han recrudecido entre Washington y Kiev desde que Trump anunciara la semana pasada un acuerdo sobre el gasóleo con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova, Daryna Krasnolutska
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Las restricciones al uso militar por parte de Ucrania del sistema Starlink de SpaceX ( SPCX ) parecen ser deliberadas y no el resultado de ningún problema técnico, afirmó el presidente Volodímir Zelenski, al tiempo que denunciaba la decisión de EE.UU. de suspender las sanciones contra Rusia. Las limitaciones de velocidad en la red de Internet Starshield siguen vigentes en toda Ucrania, lo que provoca una ralentización significativa de las conexiones, afirmó Zelenski en unos mensajes de audio enviados a los periodistas a través de WhatsApp el sábado. Tras enviar a Europa vehículos conectados a Starshield para realizar comprobaciones de velocidad y verificar que funcionaban con normalidad fuera de Ucrania, las autoridades de Kiev llegaron a la conclusión de que las restricciones “se aplican en el territorio de Ucrania, por lo que se trata de una operación planificada”, afirmó. Apenas unas horas antes, el presidente de EE.UU., Donald Trump, suspendió la aplicación de aranceles a las exportaciones energéticas rusas, impuesta en virtud de una nueva ley impulsada por el difunto senador Lindsey Graham y destinada a castigar a Rusia por su invasión de Ucrania. Rusia llevó a cabo durante la noche uno de sus mayores ataques con misiles y drones contra la infraestructura energética de Ucrania, dirigiéndose contra 15 instalaciones críticas de generación y transmisión de energía, según afirmó Zelenski. Las tensiones se han recrudecido entre Washington y Kiev desde que Trump anunciara la semana pasada un acuerdo sobre el gasóleo con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, lo que dejó atónitos a Ucrania y a sus aliados europeos. Tras las críticas de Zelenski a la decisión estadounidense, a la que calificó de débil, responsables de Defensa ucranianos señalaron esta semana que su acceso a Starshield se había ralentizado. “En el momento en que los rusos lanzaron un ataque tan masivo contra nuestro sector energético, en Estados Unidos, lamentablemente, se tomó la decisión de ignorar por completo la ley de Lindsey Graham, que se suponía que iba a ejercer una presión verdaderamente eficaz sobre Rusia para poner fin a esta guerra», escribió Zelenskyy en X. «Rusia está intentando provocar un apagón en Ucrania, justo antes del invierno», afirmó. «Un apagón de las sanciones estadounidenses, que alivia la presión sobre el agresor, y las recompensas económicas para Putin: todo ello no hace más que animarle a seguir atacando». Kiev depende de Starshield, una versión militarizada de Starlink, para que sus defensas aéreas puedan interceptar los drones propulsados por reactores que Rusia lanza a diario contra la capital de Ucrania y otras ciudades, así como para contrarrestar los ataques de artillería. La ralentización de la transmisión está obstaculizando las defensas de Ucrania y su capacidad para hacer llegar alimentos y suministros al frente, señaló Zelenski, añadiendo que la conexión de Ucrania a Starshield se interrumpe a velocidades superiores a los 161 kilómetros por hora (100 millas por hora), mientras que los drones rusos viajan a unos 400 km por hora. “Perdemos la conexión con Starlink y perdemos el interceptor”, afirmó. Estas restricciones “nos impiden defendernos y proteger a nuestra población, tanto en el frente como entre la población civil”. En sus mensajes de audio, Zelenski señaló que Ucrania estaba utilizando cazas F-16 para derribar alrededor del 60 % de los drones propulsados por motor a reacción y que se estaban entregando municiones nuevas en Kiev para reforzar las defensas aéreas. Zelenski ha acusado a Trump y a Musk de ordenar las restricciones sobre Starshield, lo que, según él, ha provocado la muerte de civiles en Ucrania. Trump afirmó el viernes que no había ordenado ninguna limitación al acceso de Ucrania al sistema y que no creía que el presidente de SpaceX, Elon Musk, lo hubiera hecho tampoco. Musk declaró el miércoles que “cualquier limitación en cuanto a velocidad o uso la decide el Ejército de EE.UU. y, en última instancia”, el presidente. Trump afirmó que tomó la decisión de invocar la cláusula de exención de la ley que firmó el mes pasado “en interés nacional de Estados Unidos”, en un decreto presidencial publicado a última hora del viernes. Si bien la directiva impone formalmente los aranceles, suspende su aplicación, lo que significa que Trump podría aplicarlos en otro momento si así lo decide. La legislación concedía al presidente de EE.UU. 30 días para imponer aranceles del 100% a todos los productos procedentes de los cinco principales compradores de crudo ruso. Asimismo, impondría sanciones a numerosas entidades rusas y aplicaría aranceles del 500% a todas las importaciones estadounidenses de productos energéticos rusos. Ese plazo de un mes estaba previsto que expirara el 18 de octubre. Esas disposiciones entran en conflicto con su plan —anunciado la semana pasada— de colaborar con Putin para liberar los suministros de gasóleo ruso en los mercados mundiales. Trump pretende reducir los precios del gasóleo en EE. UU., que se mantienen en máximos históricos a pocas semanas de las elecciones del 3 de noviembre. El enviado presidencial ruso Kirill Dmitriev, que forma parte del equipo de negociación de Putin con funcionarios estadounidenses sobre la guerra en Ucrania, elogió la decisión de Trump calificándola de «momento verdaderamente histórico» en una publicación en X. «La cooperación económica entre Rusia y Estados Unidos redunda en beneficio de ambas naciones», escribió Dmitriev. La exención de los aranceles conlleva el riesgo de una nueva reacción en contra por parte de los miembros del Congreso, incluidos muchos republicanos que se mostraron indignados por su decisión sobre el gasóleo ruso. Un grupo bipartidista de senadores firmó esta semana una carta en la que exigían a Trump que rescindiera el acuerdo con Putin y aplicara las disposiciones de la ley Graham. “Al eximir de estas sanciones, Trump está haciendo caso omiso de la indicación del Congreso de que aumente la presión sobre el Kremlin y está permitiendo que Vladimir Putin continúe con su guerra de agresión”, afirmó la senadora Elizabeth Warren en un comunicado el sábado. “Existe un firme apoyo bipartidista a Ucrania y a la exigencia de que Rusia rinda cuentas. El Congreso debería revocar el acuerdo sobre el gasóleo de Trump con Putin, reforzar el apoyo a Ucrania y tomar medidas enérgicas contra Rusia y quienes la respaldan”. Graham, republicano de Carolina del Sur y defensor de larga trayectoria de Ucrania, redactó el proyecto de ley antes de fallecer en julio, y su aprobación se consideró una forma de rendirle homenaje. Graham había calificado en repetidas ocasiones estas sanciones como la clave para llevar a Putin a la mesa de negociaciones y poner fin a su invasión a gran escala de Ucrania, que ya se encuentra en su quinto año. Rusia atacó Ucrania durante la noche con misiles balísticos y de crucero, así como con 332 drones de tipo Shahed, incluidos 31 modelos propulsados por reactores, según informó el Estado Mayor de Kiev a través de su canal de Telegram. Las fuerzas de defensa interceptaron 4 misiles de crucero Kalibr y 289 drones, según indicaron. El Ministerio de Defensa ruso afirmó en Telegram que había interceptado durante la noche 610 drones ucranianos en 16 regiones del país y en Crimea —que Putin anexionó a Rusia en 2014 a costa de Ucrania—, así como sobre el mar Negro. Putin declaró el viernes por la noche que Rusia continuará con los ataques a gran escala contra las instalaciones militar-industriales y los centros logísticos de Ucrania. Zelenski ha ordenado nuevos ataques contra refinerías de petróleo rusas, poniendo fin a una pausa en respuesta al llamamiento de Trump a una tregua energética. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Trump culpa assessores conforme pioram perspectivas dos republicanos para eleições de meio de mandato
item.description: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, está culpando assessores de alto escalão e estrategistas políticos pela estratégia vacilante para as eleições de meio de mandato, questionando os gastos com a campanha, criticando o redesenho dos distritos eleitorais e questionando as escolhas dos candidatos, enquanto os republicanos lutam para manter o controle do Congresso, afirmaram três pessoas a par das discussões internas.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Bo Erickson, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, está culpando assessores de alto escalão e estrategistas políticos pela estratégia vacilante para as eleições de meio de mandato, questionando os gastos com a campanha, criticando o redesenho dos distritos eleitorais e questionando as escolhas dos candidatos, enquanto os republicanos lutam para manter o controle do Congresso, afirmaram três pessoas a par das discussões internas. Trump não está na cédula eleitoral de 3 de novembro, mas diz repetidamente aos apoiadores para fingirem que ele está, na esperança de mobilizar eleitores que, de outra forma, poderiam deixar de votar. Ele embarcou em uma agenda frenética de campanha, ao mesmo tempo em que evita, em grande parte, reconhecer seu próprio papel na definição da estratégia e como sua impopularidade está pesando sobre os candidatos republicanos em disputas acirradas. Grande parte do atrito tem se concentrado em James Blair, o assessor de longa data que dirige o super PAC de Trump, o MAGA Inc., e na chefe de gabinete da Casa Branca, Susie Wiles, que até agora havia escapado em grande parte das críticas. Trump criticou a forma como Blair administra os fundos de campanha, enquanto alguns funcionários da Casa Branca e aliados questionaram a supervisão de Wiles sobre a operação política. Enquanto Trump questiona por que os gastos com a campanha não conseguiram melhorar os números das pesquisas dos republicanos, seus assessores também estão se culpando mutuamente. Wiles apontou Blair, enquanto Blair culpou a equipe de assuntos legislativos da Casa Branca, disse uma das pessoas. “O que está realmente acontecendo é um ‘pelotão de fuzilamento circular’”, disse a fonte. As pesquisas de opinião sugerem que os democratas conquistarão a Câmara dos Deputados, enquanto a disputa pelo Senado continua acirrada demais para se prever o resultado. Perder a Câmara prejudicaria a agenda legislativa de Trump nos dois últimos anos de seu mandato e daria aos democratas o poder de intimar testemunhas para investigar seu governo. Trump defendeu Wiles na sexta-feira, chamando-a de “inteligente” e “dura” e afirmando que ela permaneceria no cargo. “Susie está aqui e vai ficar aqui por muito tempo”, disse ele. O porta-voz da Casa Branca, Davis Ingle, rejeitou a caracterização dada pelas fontes, dizendo que se tratavam de “especialistas de poltrona divulgando suas especulações infundadas”. Wiles não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. TRUMP HÁ MUITO TEMPO SE DISTANCIA DE REVESES POLÍTICOS Trump há muito tempo busca se distanciar de reveses políticos. Ele se recusou a aceitar sua derrota nas eleições de 2020 e afirmou, antes dos resultados das eleições intermediárias de 2022, que merecia “todo o crédito” se os republicanos vencessem, mas “não deveria ser culpado de forma alguma” se perdessem. Mais recentemente, ele lembrou ao público que o partido do presidente costuma enfrentar dificuldades nas eleições intermediárias. Mas Trump ajudou a elaborar e impulsionar algumas das estratégias que agora questiona, incluindo o esforço de redistritamento e as escolhas de candidatos moldadas por suas lealdades pessoais ou queixas. O índice de aprovação de Trump está no ponto mais baixo de sua presidência, prejudicado pela preocupação dos eleitores com os preços altos e pela insatisfação com a guerra contra o Irã. US$200 MILHÕES E REDISTRIBUIÇÃO ELEITORAL Com Trump questionando por que as pesquisas dos republicanos em disputas decisivas não melhoraram, apesar dos gastos de campanha da MAGA Inc. -- que, segundo registros públicos, somam US$200 milhões até o momento --, ainda não está claro se ele aprovará mais gastos antes da eleição, disse uma das fontes. Trump também pressionou assessores políticos e consultores na última semana para que explicassem por que a iniciativa de redistribuição distrital que ele promoveu pessoalmente não conseguiu gerar ganhos republicanos mais evidentes, disseram duas fontes. O Texas é uma preocupação especial. Os republicanos redesenharam o mapa eleitoral do Estado para ganhar cadeiras, mas a estratégia depende, em parte, de que os eleitores hispânicos compareçam às urnas como fizeram na eleição de 2024. Pesquisas de opinião sugerem que esse apoio pode ser difícil de repetir em meio a preocupações com o custo de vida e com a forma como Trump tem conduzido a economia. Alguns republicanos temem que os novos limites eleitorais possam sair pela culatra, deixando os candidatos à reeleição mais vulneráveis, em vez de dar vantagem ao partido. “O redesenho distrital fragmentou demais os eleitores de Trump”, disse uma das fontes. Trump havia dito que Blair deveria retornar à Casa Branca após as eleições de meio de mandato, descrevendo sua saída como uma “breve licença”. Mas duas fontes afirmaram que seu retorno agora é improvável. “Ele não vai voltar. Isso não vai acontecer”, disse uma delas. Não estava tão claro como as coisas se desenrolariam para Wiles, que desempenhou um papel central na vitória de Trump em 2024 e a quem os aliados e assessores de Trump atribuem o mérito de ter trazido maior disciplina à Casa Branca em seu segundo mandato. Trump “pode estar incomodado com certas coisas, mas ela tem mantido essa máquina funcionando de forma eficaz”, disse uma quarta fonte próxima à Casa Branca. (Reportagem de Nandita Bose, Steve Holland e Bo Erickson, em Washington; Reportagem adicional de Trevor Hunnicutt e Alexandra Ulmer)

item.title: Barcola shines as Liverpool labour to 2-1 win over Brentford
item.description: Liverpool bounced back from last week’s 3-0 Premier League drubbing by Manchester City with a workmanlike 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday, as winger Bradley Barcola showcased the full range of his talents despite spurning two gilt-edged chances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Liverpool bounced back from last week’s [USN:L8N45X08M TEXT:"3-0 Premier League drubbing by Manchester City"] with a workmanlike 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday, as winger Bradley Barcola showcased the full range of his talents despite spurning two gilt-edged chances. Keane Lewis-Potter had given the home side the lead in the 44th minute but Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off for an attempted headbutt deep into first-half stoppage time, and Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak completed Liverpool's comeback with second-half goals to seal the three points. "Super-happy with the win. It's a tough ground, it's a tough team to play, especially away from home. We knew it was going to be a bit of a scrappy game and it's important to come out on top," Isak said. Vitaly Janelt picked up a second yellow card in stoppage time to leave Brentford with nine men, and Barcola then squandered another opportunity when he opted to pass rather than shoot after Liverpool broke forward on the counter-attack. Perhaps his mind was still on his first-half opportunity, when he intercepted Janelt’s attempted header and raced clear, only to lift his effort over the onrushing goalkeeper and wide. Either way, the two chances gave Liverpool fans a glimpse of what may be to come once he settles fully on Merseyside. Signed from Paris St Germain in a deal [USN:L4N44Q01S TEXT:"worth up to 123 million pounds"], the 24-year-old was a constant threat from his starting position on the left wing, cutting inside onto his right foot to shoot or cross and moving infield or up front whenever the opportunity arose. With opponents often deploying five players across the back against the leading sides, Barcola’s skill, agility and trickery offer Liverpool another means of unlocking compact defences following Mohamed Salah’s departure at the end of last season. "I think there's still lots to improve. We're taking steps and we're grabbing points on the way which is important. It's a tough place to come, so three points is really good," Isak said.

item.title: Italian police clash with protesters in Milan and Bologna
item.description: Police fired tear gas on Saturday after coming under attack from protesters throwing stones in the square in front of Milan's Gothic cathedral, Italian media reported, while there were also clashes in the city of Bologna following protests over the cost of living.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Police fired tear gas on Saturday after coming under attack from protesters throwing stones in the square in front of Milan's Gothic cathedral, Italian media reported, while there were also clashes in the city of Bologna following protests over the cost of living. Police in Bologna used a water cannon to try to disperse crowds and made seven arrests after the protest became violent, the ANSA news agency reported. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, facing an election next year, condemned the violence. "Demonstrating is a right. Turning our cities into battlegrounds is not," she said on X. In Milan, police in riot gear also tried to clear hooded protesters from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the luxury shopping arcade on one side of the cathedral square, as groups broke away from the cost-of-living protest. Shops pulled down their shutters and tourists fled the central area. The central Duomo (Cathedral) metro station was closed during the clashes in which several people were reported injured, and arrests were made, according to the Italian media reports. The clashes echoed the violence [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"in neighbouring France,"] where tens of thousands of people, angered by rising costs and declining public services, took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years.

item.title: India, West Indies draw T20 series after rain washes out decider
item.description: India and West Indies had to settle for a 2-2 draw in their five-match T20 series after the fifth and deciding game ended with no result due to rain on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India and West Indies had to settle for a 2-2 draw in their five-match T20 series after the fifth and deciding game ended with no result due to rain on Saturday. Persistent showers delayed the start and reduced the contest to nine overs per side before West Indies won the toss and elected to field. India lost opener Abhishek Sharma for six off the bowling of Keemo Paul but Ishan Kishan then hammered 30 off 10 balls to provide the early impetus. The hosts surged to 118-5 in 7.4 overs but rain returned before the innings could be completed, forcing the players off the field. With conditions failing to improve, officials ended the match and both teams shared the series honours. The match was the first international fixture at Chinnaswamy Stadium in two years. Veteran seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar, recalled to India's T20 squad for the first time since November 2022, was denied the chance to mark his return with the ball.

item.title: Maple Leafs F John Tavares (lower body) is week-to-week
item.description: The Toronto Maple Leafs listed forward John Tavares as week-to-week with a lower-body injury on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Toronto Maple Leafs listed forward John Tavares as week-to-week with a lower-body injury on Saturday. The designation means the 36-year-old veteran could be sidelined for up to six weeks, according to The Athletic. Tavares exited Thursday's game against Buffalo after a collision with Sabres forward Joshua Norris. Tavares has seven points (two goals, five assists) in seven games this season, his ninth with Toronto and 18th in the NHL. He has 1,192 points (527 goals, 665 assists) in 1,273 career games with the Islanders (2009-18) and Maple Leafs since New York drafted him No. 1 overall in 2009. --Field Level Media

item.title: Colts activate TE Will Mallory from IR
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts activated Will Mallory from injured reserve on Saturday, one day after they listed fellow tight end Tyler Warren as questionable with a groin injury that he sustained in practice.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts activated Will Mallory from injured reserve on Saturday, one day after they listed fellow tight end Tyler Warren as questionable with a groin injury that he sustained in practice. Mallory's questionable status was lifted from the injury report by the Colts (2-3) ahead of Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans (0-5) in Indianapolis. He had been on injured reserve since Aug. 30 with a thumb injury. Mallory, 27, has 23 catches for 252 yards in 24 career games (two starts) with the Colts. He was selected by Indianapolis in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Miami. A Pro Bowl selection in his rookie season in 2025, Warren has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns in five games (all starts) this season. Warren, 24, also has a touchdown run. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tens of thousands march in Lisbon over housing and living costs
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on Saturday to protest against soaring living costs and a deepening housing crisis in Portugal, increasing pressure on the centre-right government.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on Saturday to protest against soaring living costs and a deepening housing crisis in Portugal, increasing pressure on the centre-right government. Portugal's biggest union, CGTP, which called the rally, said "many tens of thousands" packed one of the capital's main avenues. Police gave no crowd estimate. Protesters say low wages are failing to keep pace with housing costs and the rising cost of living, leaving many people struggling to make ends meet in the European Union and NATO member state. The demonstration followed days of growing unrest, including a tent camp set up by housing activists in the northern city of Porto that police cleared in a pre-dawn operation on Monday. It coincides with [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"protests in France"] against rising costs and declining public services, and smaller protests in [USN:L6N46303L TEXT:"Belgium"]. There are also mass protests in [USN:L6N46303U TEXT:"Albania"], where protesters are demanding the prime minister's resignation. Portugal's [USN:APNAL1YR5 TEXT:"inflation hit 3.6% in September"], driven by rising food and fuel prices, the latter up 15% year-on-year following an increase in tensions in the Middle East. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, fuelling one of Europe's worst housing affordability crises. The squeeze is most acute in major cities. PROTESTERS' CONCERNS Carolina Cruz, 26, a PhD student and biology researcher earning about €1,300 ($1,460) a month on a scholarship, faces losing her home as her rental contract nears expiry. She and her partner pay €716 monthly for an apartment in the Lisbon area, but renewal could push the rent above €1,200 — far beyond their means. "I'm the first person in my family to enter a doctoral programme, and even with all the studying I've done, I still can't make it... Right now, housing in Lisbon is the problem," Cruz said. Pedro Penilo, 62, a teacher, said Portugal's leaders were "out of touch with reality." "Life is incredibly expensive… it's going up brutally. I need to see how my mortgage is going to turn out in the coming months, when it's adjusted. I'm very worried," he said. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos Abreu Amorim said on Friday the "government will not yield to shouts from the street" and that [USN:L8N3X91P8 TEXT:"concrete measures"] to address the concerns were already being rolled out. ($1 = 0.8898 euros)

item.title: Des Palestiniens et des responsables européens attaqués par des colons en Cisjordanie occupée
item.description: Des colons juifs masqués ont attaqué des Palestiniens, des représentants de l'Eglise catholique et des responsables européens en Cisjordanie occupée, a annoncé samedi le ministre belge des Affaires étrangères.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des colons juifs masqués ont attaqué des Palestiniens, des représentants de l'Eglise catholique et des responsables européens en Cisjordanie occupée, a annoncé samedi le ministre belge des Affaires étrangères. Maxime Prévot a précisé que le consul général de Belgique, des diplomates français et polonais ainsi qu’un maire français figuraient parmi les personnes agressées, et qu’un véhicule belge avait été endommagé. "Récolter des olives, couvrir l’actualité ou exercer des fonctions diplomatiques ne devrait jamais exposer quiconque au risque d’une agression", a dénoncé le chef de la diplomatie belge. Bernard Baudoux, maire d'Aulnoye-Aymeries, dans le Nord de la France, a déclaré à Reuters qu'il récoltait des olives avec des habitants du village majoritairement chrétien de Taybeh lorsqu'il a été "violemment agressé" par des colons. "J'ai été jeté au sol", a-t-il dit. Le ministre israélien des Affaires étrangères, Gideon Sarr, a condamné l'attaque, qu'il a imputée sur la plateforme X à des "émeutiers israéliens", tout en critiquant le fait que le déplacement des responsables européens n'ait pas été coordonné avec les autorités israéliennes. Maxime Prévot a déclaré de son côté que la Belgique continuerait à faire pression pour que des sanctions soient prises à l’encontre des responsables de ces violences et de ceux qui les soutiennent. "En tant que puissance occupante, les autorités israéliennes doivent protéger les Palestiniens, garantir la sécurité des diplomates et des journalistes, et traduire les responsables en justice. Il faut mettre fin à l'impunité dont bénéficient les colons violents", a-t-il écrit sur X. Cette attaque est intervenue au lendemain de l'agression par des colons de la photo-journaliste américaine Heidi Levine, qui couvrait la récolte des olives pour le Washington Post.

item.title: Chelsea's Martinez undergoes surgery after collision at Everton
item.description: Emi Martinez has undergone surgery following his collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, the Chelsea goalkeeper said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emi Martinez has undergone surgery following his collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, the Chelsea goalkeeper said on Sunday, after his club's [USN:L1N463054 TEXT:"2-0 Premier League victory."] Pedro Neto's double on Saturday at the Hill Dickinson Stadium ended Everton's unbeaten start to the league season, but Chelsea's victory was overshadowed by the lengthy injury stoppage in the second half. Martinez and Branthwaite came together when Everton's Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall whipped a free kick into the box and, although the defender was back on his feet after treatment, the Argentina goalkeeper required treatment from paramedics. The 34-year-old was eventually strapped to a stretcher and carried off the field before being taken to hospital with a concussion, as Argentine media reported he had suffered a jaw injury in the collision. Martinez, wearing a hospital gown, posted on social media early on Sunday: "Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well. "The most important thing is that we won, and kept a clean sheet. In a few weeks we'll be back." Martinez's injury forced Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso to give Mike Penders his Premier League debut, and the 21-year-old keeper helped Chelsea keep their first clean sheet in the league since January. Penders, a Belgian youth international, will likely have to step in until Martinez is cleared to return to training. Chelsea host Tottenham Hotspur in the league next Saturday followed by a League Cup fourth-round game at Liverpool on October 28 and a home Premier League match against Manchester United three days later. "Mike has personality. He's brave and we have full trust with him. He did well," Alonso told reporters. "He played in the cup games and whenever he's needed, like the other players whenever they are needed they can perform. "It's all about the squad, that all the players feel important and can have their moment whenever they are needed, and that's very positive."

item.title: Guarda Revolucionária do Irã afirma que dois petroleiros atingiram minas no Estreito de Ormuz
item.description: A Marinha da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã informou neste sábado que dois petroleiros pegaram fogo após colidirem com minas navais enquanto atravessavam o Estreito de Ormuz, segundo noticiou a agência oficial de notícias iraniana Irna.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Marinha da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã informou neste sábado que dois petroleiros pegaram fogo após colidirem com minas navais enquanto atravessavam o Estreito de Ormuz, segundo noticiou a agência oficial de notícias iraniana Irna. A mídia estatal informou que ambos os petroleiros transportavam cerca de 2 milhões de barris de petróleo bruto. Não houve confirmação independente das notícias. A Irna informou que as embarcações haviam desligado seus sistemas de posicionamento e radar e tentaram usar uma rota não autorizada pela via navegável estratégica. A segunda embarcação ficou imobilizada após colidir com uma mina, acrescentou a agência. A mídia estatal havia informado anteriormente que o outro petroleiro também havia colidido com uma mina ao tentar atravessar o estreito por uma rota não autorizada pelo Irã. Os incidentes ocorrem em meio a tensões crescentes em torno do estreito, uma rota fundamental para o transporte de petróleo. As interrupções na navegação na via, decorrentes da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, impulsionaram os preços globais da energia e a inflação. Autoridades marítimas informaram na quarta-feira que um navio porta-contêineres e um graneleiro [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"afundaram"] perto do estreito após serem atingidos por projéteis em incidentes separados.
